dedupe_keys.name: review into the optus outage of 8 november 2023 bean review

description: This post-incident review examines the national Optus outage of 8 November 2023, which began at about 04:05 AEDT, lasted roughly twelve hours and cut mobile, fixed internet and landline services for about 10 million people and 400,000 businesses in Australia, leaving some customers unable to call the 000 emergency number and disrupting hospitals, payments and transport. Optus attributed it to around 90 provider-edge routers disconnecting as a protective measure after routing updates from a Singtel exchange overseas exceeded preset limits following a software upgrade. The Australian Government appointed Richard Bean, a former deputy chair of the Australian Communications and Media Authority, to lead the review on 9 November 2023; its final report of 21 March 2024 made 18 recommendations on emergency call arrangements, customer communications, complaints handling and compensation, and the government published its response in April 2024. Coverage: Australia-wide, one event. Format and access: web page with the final report and government response as free PDF downloads. Caveats: it focuses on lessons for industry and government, not full technical reconstruction; figures on affected users come from the operator. Simulation uses: a reference case for cascading failure in a national carrier, dependency of emergency calls and other sectors on telecommunications, emergency response planning and policy evaluation. Related records: the Rogers 2022 CRTC review covers a similar event in Canada, and IODA and Cloudflare Radar recorded the outage.
